sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: No phonology of Bapen. Bapen cited as a comparandum: p. 13 (Tenda subgroup membership), p. 13-14 mutation-grade discussion ('Basari d II ~ Konyagi nt III: sorghum: Basari dəli II ~ Konyagi væ̀-ntəlí III (Bapen ɓɛ-ndʌɗi / ɛ- III)'), p. 315-316 basic-lexicon reconstructions (Bapen ɛ-kaɲ / mo-haɲ 'stone', a-cʌɗ / ɓa- 'bird', ɛ-tʌnd / mɔ-sʌnd 'hill'). Bapen forms carry no tone marks (Basari e-kàỹ, Konyagi wæ̀-səry next to them do). No statement on Bapen or Tenda prosody; the book's only 'tone' mentions are general.

sources.citation: Pozdniakov, Konstantin. 2018. The numeral system of Proto-Niger-Congo: A step-by-step reconstruction (Niger-Congo Comparative Studies 2). Berlin: Language Science Press. (OAPEN 20.500.12657/28278)

Bapen forms are printed without tone marks while adjacent Basari forms carry them; nothing is said about Bapen (or Tenda) tone or stress. Useful pointers in its references: Pozdniakov 2…
